tasks.short: Answer employee and applicant questions about examinations, eligibility, salaries, benefits and HR procedures.

steps.what: Read the question and verify identity, scope and access rights.
Look up relevant employee or applicant facts.
Find current policies, benefit rules and examination guidance.
Combine personnel facts and guidance into a proposed answer.

loop.input: Authorised question, permitted personnel facts and current approved guidance.
loop.output: Draft answer with source references and explicit unresolved points.
loop.check: Validate source versions, references and numerical fields; reject unsupported entitlement conclusions.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair attempt; missing or conflicting support routes to an HR specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover fixed questions; varied wording and contextual explanations need bounded drafting.

steps.what: Resolve ambiguous eligibility or policy interpretations when needed.
Check the answer, send it and record the response.

tasks.design: An authenticated answer desk in the {WORKFLOW} retrieves permitted facts from the {HCM} or {ATS} and current guidance from the {DOCS}. Fixed answers use templates; a bounded drafting loop prepares contextual replies with references. An HR specialist approves ambiguous interpretations, and the HR assistant approves release through the {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Guidance, personal facts and correspondence sit separately. Maintaining current guidance and access rights takes more effort than building a search box.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing self-service and knowledge features cover much of the flow. AI-assisted coding reduces connector and validation work; bounded drafting handles varied wording.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting agreements, individual exceptions and outdated guidance remain difficult. GDPR access controls, EU AI Act classification and applicable national rules need assessment when the scope changes.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a factual question hides distress, a dispute or a request for discretion.

ambition.what: An employee benefit-change explainer using approved personal facts.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts toward difficult questions and repairing confusing guidance. No entitlement decision rights change; a delegated role could propose guidance changes from recurring questions.

reach.learn: Effective dates, agreement precedence and when an explanation becomes an entitlement decision.

evidence.claim: HR self-service and answers grounded in employment agreements are available capabilities.
Knowledge-based answers can hand unresolved questions to a pre-filled request.
Personalised salary and eligibility replies need access restrictions and controlled release.

assumptions: Step shares and remaining time are planning estimates, not measured results.
The employer has searchable guidance and employee records with identifiable effective dates.
Specialist handling is conditional; its share represents time across a typical mix of inquiries.
The final handoff includes applicants; employee replies remain internal.
Build ranges are working-day effort for one deployment. Access includes consultation under national rules where applicable; elapsed waiting time may be longer.
unknowns: Which guidance is approved, current and owned?
Which inquiry types require specialist interpretation?
Can existing authentication and record permissions be reused?
Which consultation and access approvals apply locally?
research_questions: How reliably do existing knowledge features filter guidance by agreement and effective date?
Which additional EU AI Act obligations apply if the scope moves from explanation into employment decisions?
new_work: Review drafted replies and resolve unsupported statements.
Maintain guidance versions, answer templates and escalation routes.
Investigate access failures and sample released answers for accuracy.

tasks.short: Prepare orientation schedules, materials, invitations and rooms for new employees.

steps.what: Check confirmed starters, locations and recorded preparation requirements.
Coordinate presenters, rooms and session times.
Assemble agendas, welcome materials and required learning links.
Send joining instructions and request room and equipment preparation.
Arrange the room, place materials and test presentation equipment.
Check readiness and resolve last-minute changes with presenters and starters.

tasks.design: A starter event from the {HCM} triggers a configured schedule in the {WORKFLOW} using the {CALENDAR}. A deterministic generator assembles approved materials from the {DOCS} and links from the {LMS}, then sends joining instructions and setup requests through the {EMAIL} and {HELPDESK}. People prepare the physical space and resolve individual needs.
tasks.previous_blocker: Starter changes, calendar availability and material versions require repeated coordination across teams.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing workflow triggers, shared calendars and document templates provide the core. Small integrations can connect them without a model.
tasks.still_hard: Physical preparation, unavailable presenters and late accessibility requests still need people. Record only necessary accommodation information and follow GDPR and applicable national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Notice whether the setting will help a particular starter feel welcome and able to participate.

ambition.what: Equivalent orientation preparation for remote and satellite-site starters.

tasks.altitude: The assistant spends less time assembling packs and chasing routine bookings. With delegation, they can adjust session formats within an approved orientation programme.

reach.task: Adapt induction materials for different learning and access needs.
reach.learn: Accessible formats, learning objectives and how to evaluate starter understanding.

evidence.claim: Calendar coordination, template assembly and setup requests can use deterministic workflows.
Physical room setup and individual readiness checks remain human work.

assumptions: Step shares and remaining time are planning estimates, not measured results.
Orientation uses a repeatable programme with approved materials and named presenters.
The roster contains confirmed contact details; joining instructions contain no sensitive personnel facts.
Shares cover the preparation process, including workplace-team effort; they are not all HR-assistant hours.
Build ranges are working-day effort. Access includes consultation under national rules where applicable; elapsed waiting time may be longer.
unknowns: Can starter events and room availability be accessed through existing configuration?
Who approves orientation templates and permissible schedule changes?
How often do start dates, locations and access requirements change?
research_questions: Can the existing scheduling configuration handle cancellations and duplicate starter events safely?
new_work: Maintain starter-to-session rules and approved material versions.
Handle scheduling conflicts and failed invitations.
Check room-request completion and update remote participation instructions.

tasks.short: Collect required personnel records from employees and departments, check completeness and file them.

steps.what: Identify required records for the employee event.
Find records already held by HR and other departments.
Request missing records from employees or departmental owners.
Receive submitted records and record receipt.
Check document identity, dates, completeness and apparent inconsistencies.

loop.input: Submitted documents, required fields and permitted employee identifiers.
loop.output: Document type, cited field values and completeness exceptions.
loop.check: Validate identifiers, date formats and required fields against the checklist; a person reviews uncertain matches.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per document; unreadable or conflicting documents enter the exception queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Forms need only fixed validation; varied legacy documents require bounded text extraction.

steps.what: Chase outstanding records and clarify incomplete submissions.
Attach accepted records to the employee file and close the collection checklist.

tasks.design: An event in the {HCM} selects a required-record checklist and reuses permitted records from the {HCM}, {LMS} and {DOCS}. Configured self-service uploads replace attachment handling, while a bounded extraction loop checks legacy documents for review. The {WORKFLOW} sends capped reminders, routes exceptions and files accepted records with an audit trail.
tasks.previous_blocker: Record requirements and ownership vary by event. Mail attachments lack reliable identifiers, and departments keep separate copies.
tasks.enabler_now: Self-service capture and deterministic record matching cover the main flow. Bounded extraction reduces manual inspection of varied documents.
tasks.still_hard: Missing records still require their owners to act. Authenticity, disputed facts, special-category data and retention rules need human handling under GDPR and applicable national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Understand why someone cannot provide a record and agree a legitimate alternative without collecting unnecessary information.

ambition.what: A pre-action personnel-record readiness check for HR specialists.

tasks.altitude: The assistant spends more time resolving evidence gaps before employment changes are delayed. No employment decision rights change; delegated discretion could cover requesting approved alternative evidence.

reach.task: Check whether personnel evidence supports a proposed contract change.
reach.learn: Evidence sufficiency, agreement requirements and escalation for disputed records.

evidence.claim: HR self-service can collect changes and route them into connected employee administration.
Document extraction with rule checks and exception routing is an available pattern; HR-specific validation needs testing.
Existing records can be reused through permission-controlled references instead of repeated collection.

assumptions: Step shares and remaining time are planning estimates, not measured results.
Shares measure collection administration; employees' time finding or producing missing evidence is excluded.
The checklist specifies permitted record types, required fields and retention rules.
The model checks document content, not authenticity or employment eligibility.
Reminders stop after two attempts and escalate unresolved cases.
Build ranges are working-day effort. Access includes consultation under national rules where applicable; elapsed waiting time may be longer.
unknowns: Which employee events trigger each checklist?
Where are authoritative records held and who may access them?
What proportion of submissions use structured forms versus varied documents?
Which records require specialist verification or restricted storage?
research_questions: What extraction accuracy can representative redacted personnel documents support?
Can existing self-service preserve document versions and prevent duplicate filing?
new_work: Review uncertain document matches and disputed submissions.
Maintain checklists, record ownership and reminder schedules.
Repair failed transfers and audit duplicate or incorrectly retained records.

tasks.short: Search employee files and provide authorised facts for inquiries and personnel actions.

steps.what: Read the inquiry and clarify the facts needed.
Verify the requester's authority and permitted information scope.
Retrieve relevant dates, roles, contract fields and recorded changes.
Read relevant contracts, letters and supporting employee-file documents.

loop.input: Authorised question and permission-filtered employee-file documents.
loop.output: Relevant factual extracts with document, page and effective-date references.
loop.check: Confirm quotations against source text and validate employee identity and document version.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt; absent or conflicting evidence is returned as unresolved.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured fields use direct lookup; facts in varied historical letters need contextual extraction.

steps.what: Reconcile conflicting records and identify facts requiring specialist confirmation.
Check disclosure scope, send the fact brief and record the disclosure.

tasks.design: A request form in the {WORKFLOW} checks identity and disclosure scope before retrieving structured facts from the {HCM}. Permission-filtered documents from the {DOCS} feed a bounded extraction loop, and a deterministic generator assembles a cited fact brief. The HR assistant resolves conflicts and approves disclosure; the brief supports a separately authorised personnel decision.
tasks.previous_blocker: Structured records and historical letters disagree or use different dates. Broad folder access makes safe retrieval harder than simple search.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing record views can answer structured questions directly. Small integrations and cited text extraction reduce document reading and brief assembly.
tasks.still_hard: Historical contradictions and unclear authority cannot be settled by retrieval. GDPR purpose limits, sensitive records, EU AI Act scope and applicable national rules remain relevant.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a documented fact from an inference and recognise when releasing a true fact would still be inappropriate.

ambition.what: An evidence brief showing effective dates and unresolved conflicts before contract changes.

tasks.altitude: The assistant becomes a stronger evidence partner for HR specialists and spends less time searching files. Employment decision rights do not change; disputed facts still need authorised resolution.

reach.task: Build an evidence chronology for a disputed personnel action.
reach.learn: Source provenance, neutral chronology, confidentiality and the boundary between fact and interpretation.

evidence.claim: Existing HR systems support employee records and self-service information flows.
Permission-filtered retrieval and source-cited extraction can support factual briefs without deciding personnel actions.
Record conflicts and disclosure scope need explicit handling before information is released.

assumptions: Step shares and remaining time are planning estimates, not measured results.
Most requests seek internal factual information rather than legal advice.
The request form replaces much of mailbox clarification; unusual requests still need a person.
Retrieval permissions are enforced before document content reaches the model.
Unresolved conflicts remain visible and are not silently resolved by document recency.
Build ranges are working-day effort. Access includes consultation under national rules where applicable; elapsed waiting time may be longer.
unknowns: Are document permissions as granular as employee-record permissions?
Which source prevails for each personnel field and effective date?
Who may resolve conflicting records or approve unusual disclosures?
How much of the archive is searchable and correctly indexed?
research_questions: Can retrieval preserve document-level permissions across both current files and archives?
How accurately can extraction distinguish signed amendments from superseded drafts?
new_work: Review cited extracts and investigate conflicting records.
Maintain field ownership, disclosure rules and permission mappings.
Audit disclosure logs and correct indexing or source-version errors.

role.altitude: The week shifts from searching, chasing and assembling toward evidence quality, difficult inquiries and starter readiness. Greater authority requires explicit delegation; these changes do not confer employment decision rights.
reach: HR specialists: prepare evidence for contract changes.
Compensation and benefits specialists: explain eligibility exceptions.
Training and development specialists: improve accessible induction preparation.
Labor relations specialists: assemble neutral personnel chronologies.
skills_to_grow: Effective dates, source precedence and personnel evidence quality.
GDPR-aware access, disclosure and retention practices.
Workflow configuration, exception handling and integration monitoring.
Checking source-cited model outputs without accepting unsupported conclusions.
Accessible communication and sensitive employee conversations.
role.ambitious_version: An HR operations evidence partner who provides timely, permission-controlled facts and spots recurring preparation gaps before they delay employee changes or onboarding.

job.title: Human Resources Assistants, Except Payroll and Timekeeping
